blocks.text: Faceless workers and a tsunami of Post-it notes: the surreal world of Japan’s salarymen – in pictures

In his photographic series Ganbatte, Copenhagen-based Argentinian visual artist Jairo Alvarez explores the juxtaposition and harmony between Japan’s relentless work culture and its traditions, connection to nature and faith.
The exhibition features as part of the Head On photo festival 2026 on the Bondi beach promenade from 6 to 29 November
Ganbatte is a Japanese term meaning ‘do your best’ or ‘keep going’. It is used to encourage and uplift others, particularly during challenging moments. Photograph: Jairo Alvarez

blocks.alt: A headless suit stands before a screen, evoking the Japanese salaryman who has “evaporated”

blocks.text: Jōhatsu is a Japanese term meaning ‘evaporation’. It refers to people who suddenly disappear from their lives, leaving jobs, families and identities behind, often due to social pressures, debt or a desire to start over anonymously

blocks.alt: A salaryman’s suit is wrapped in snakeskin-patterned fabric outside Shinjuku-nishiguchi station
A digital clock reads 6:00 beside glasses and omamori charms on a bedside table

blocks.text: Omamori is a Japanese term referring to amulets or talismans that are often sold at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples in Japan. These amulets are believed to provide various forms of protection or good luck to the bearer. The word

omamori itself can be translated as ‘protection’ or ‘charm’. They are typically displayed and sold at small stands or counters, often near the main hall or entrance of a shrine or temple, where visitors can see and choose from different types of
omamori depending on the blessing they seek

blocks.alt: A silhouetted salaryman stands before a glowing red sun framed by window blinds
A kneeling salaryman in a pinstripe suit sits beside a coffee cup and its disassembled lid parts

blocks.text: sadō (the way of tea) is a traditional ritual centred on the preparation and sharing of matcha (powdered green tea). Rooted in Zen Buddhist philosophy, it emphasises harmony, respect, purity and tranquility through the host’s deliberate movements and the guests’ mindful attention. Every element, from the utensils to the seasonal decorations, is chosen to create a moment of quiet simplicity

blocks.alt: Small black cups stacked in a pyramid on a bar table beside beer mugs and a sake bottle

blocks.text: nomu (meaning ‘to drink’) with ‘communication’ and reflects the tradition of forging connections over drinks. Over time, this practice has shaped workplace dynamics and, consequently, recruitment strategies

blocks.alt: A businessman sits on the floor, gazing up at wave-shaped sticky notes resembling the Great Wave
Tokyo office tower at night, with lit windows forming a sad face shape
A sleeping salaryman rests his chin on chopsticks balanced upright on a counter

blocks.text: ganbatte reflects the importance of perseverance and collective support. It serves as a reminder to individuals that their efforts are recognised and that they have the strength to overcome difficulties and achieve their goals
